carnage.name: MashedBROtato
carnage.commentary: Eleven on a par-4 is pure archaeological golf: you don’t play the hole, you excavate it. That kind of number usually means the ball spent more time in witness protection than in play.

carnage.name: derekldavis
carnage.commentary: Eleven on a par-4 is a full-blown equipment grievance. When a hole eats that many shots, the only thing that stayed on schedule was the suffering.

players.name: MashedBROtato
players.tagline: The putter tried to save the round; the short game dragged it behind the shed.
players.body: This was a familiar kind of beatdown with one weird bright spot: MashedBROtato finished seventh in both nets and gross, but the round never stopped bleeding where it mattered. The tee game was actually the least offensive part, and the putter chipped in enough to keep the corpse twitching, but the short game absolutely torched the scorecard. Four sand chances, zero saves, four three-putts, and an 11-shot disaster on 15 are how you turn a round into a tax audit. That’s the story again for him: the upside is real enough to show up, but the bottom half of the bag keeps kicking the chair out from under it.

players.name: derekldavis
players.tagline: Driver was a liability, and the rest of the bag had to fight uphill in mud.
players.body: derekldavis came in eighth in both nets and gross, and the round looked exactly like the numbers suggest: the tee ball was a crime scene, the putter was the only thing that showed up with a pulse, and everything else spent the day looking for a way to survive. The damage started early and never really left, with an 11 on 6 and another ugly blowup on 7 turning the round into a hostage situation. The longer view is brutal but consistent: this is now a five-start profile of getting carved up off the tee and not nearly enough from the rest of the bag to patch it together. The putter kept this from being even uglier, which is basically handing out paper towels in a house fire.
